name: Basic Vehicle
description:
Drivable vehicle with throttle/steer input, top speed, and seat-based entry/exit.

HOW IT MOVES IS A DECLARED CHOICE, because the genres that use this want different answers and a constant standing between them decides for both. A freight train on transport_tycoon's network moves tile to tile along a route; a car in driving_racing has a heading and slides when it corners too fast, and the whole feel of that genre is in the sliding. Neither is a better vehicle — they are different vehicles, and this component owned only the first because grid stepping was what the runtime could do.

`stepped` is the default so nothing that already drives one changes. `continuous` integrates through movement.physics_core's `planar`, which is where the arithmetic lives, and publishes `heading` and `velocity` for movement.vehicle_tuning and progression.drift_scoring to read. Under `stepped` those two are absent rather than zero: a vehicle that cannot slide has no drift to report, and reporting 0 would make a drift score look earned.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.
Upstream module named; no adapter written.

inputs.name: motion
inputs.description: `stepped` moves a tile at a time at a rate set by topSpeed — right for rail, grids and anything routed. `continuous` gives the vehicle a heading and a velocity and integrates them, which is what cornering, drifting and ramming all need. An unknown value falls back to `stepped` rather than failing, because a typo in a handling model should not stop a game booting.

outputs.name: heading
outputs.description: Facing in radians. Published only under `continuous` — a stepped vehicle has no heading distinct from the direction it last moved.

outputs.name: velocity
outputs.description: `{x, y}` in world units per second, under `continuous` only. progression.drift_scoring reads this against `heading` to find the lateral component.
